concept.name: Online Schema Migrations

relationships.description: Connects Online Schema Migrations to database indexing in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Techniques for altering tables, indexes, and constraints on live production databases without taking downtime or blocking application reads and writes.
spark.keyTakeaway: Never run a blocking `ALTER TABLE` directly on a large table; pair the Expand-and-Contract pattern with online shadow-table tools (`gh-ost`) or Postgres lock-safe primitives (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `lock_timeout`).

concept.whyItMatters: A naive `ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN tax_cents BIGINT NOT NULL` or `DROP COLUMN` can acquire an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` or metadata lock (MDL) that stalls every `SELECT`, `INSERT`, and `UPDATE` behind it. On a 200M-row table, a 20-minute table rewrite exhausts your application's connection pool in seconds and triggers a site-wide outage.
whenToUse: Altering tables exceeding a few million rows or several gigabytes in MySQL/InnoDB or PostgreSQL where table rewrites take minutes to hours.
Zero-downtime deployments using rolling or blue/green releases where old (v1) and new (v2) application pods run concurrently against the same schema.
High-throughput OLTP tables (>1,000 QPS) where even a 5-second metadata lock queue causes cascading API timeouts.
whenNotToUse: Brand-new or empty tables with zero production traffic where an instant DDL statement finishes in <10 milliseconds.
Offline data warehouses or batch-only staging tables that have scheduled maintenance windows.
PostgreSQL 11+ `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT <constant>` (non-volatile) without a rewrite—Postgres handles this in O(1) metadata time, though you still need a tight `lock_timeout`.
keyPoints: Expand-and-Contract separates a breaking change into backward-compatible steps: add new schema, dual-write, backfill, switch reads, then drop old schema.
In PostgreSQL, `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` avoids blocking writes, while `ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID` followed by `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` avoids holding `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` during full-table scans.
Always set `SET lock_timeout = '2s'` before running Postgres DDL so a blocked migration fails fast instead of queuing behind a long-running analytics query and starving all incoming traffic.
In MySQL, tools like `gh-ost` (triggerless binlog streaming) and `pt-online-schema-change` (trigger-based) copy rows into a shadow table in throttled chunks and cut over via an atomic `RENAME TABLE`.
Replica lag monitoring is mandatory: online backfills and shadow copies must throttle or pause automatically when replication lag exceeds thresholds (e.g., 50–100ms).

examples.title: Splitting a Monolithic `users.full_name` Column in MySQL with gh-ost
examples.scenario: A 180M-row `users` table (95 GB) needed `first_name` and `last_name` columns added and backfilled without stalling 12,000 QPS of login and profile traffic.
examples.outcome: Using `gh-ost` with `--max-lag-millis=50` and `--chunk-size=2000`, the team copied the table over 4.5 hours during off-peak traffic, dual-wrote in app code for 48 hours, and executed an atomic cutover with p99 latency remaining under 18ms.

examples.title: Eliminating a Lock Queue Outage in PostgreSQL 15
examples.scenario: An engineer ran `ALTER TABLE invoices ADD CONSTRAINT fk_org FOREIGN KEY (org_id) REFERENCES orgs(id)` without a `lock_timeout`. A 40-second BI query held `ACCESS SHARE`, causing the `ALTER` to wait—and blocking 400+ incoming `SELECT`s behind it.
examples.outcome: Switching to `SET lock_timeout = '2s'`, adding the constraint `NOT VALID` (instant metadata lock), and running `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` (takes only `SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE`, allowing reads and writes) eliminated lock-queue outages.

tradeOffs.pro: Zero-downtime rollouts with safe rollback at every phase (v1 and v2 code both work).
tradeOffs.con: A single column rename or type change expands from 1 PR into 3–4 sequential PRs across days.

tradeOffs.pro: `gh-ost` avoids `INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` trigger overhead on the primary and can dynamically pause on replica lag.
tradeOffs.con: `gh-ost` requires row-based replication (`binlog_format=ROW`) and cannot easily migrate tables with foreign keys pointing to them.

tradeOffs.pro: Shadow tables keep the live table untouched until the final millisecond swap.
tradeOffs.con: Requires at least 2x free disk space for the table being migrated and consumes extra IOPS during chunk copying.

failureModes.name: Postgres Lock-Queue Pileup
failureModes.description: An `ALTER TABLE` needing `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` waits behind a slow `SELECT`. Every subsequent `SELECT` or `UPDATE` queues behind the waiting `ALTER`, exhausting connection pools in seconds.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce `SET lock_timeout = '2000ms'` and `SET statement_timeout = '5000ms'` in migration runners, retrying with backoff if a lock cannot be acquired.

failureModes.name: Replication Lag Spike During Backfill
failureModes.description: Unthrottled `UPDATE` batches or shadow-table copies saturate replica I/O, causing read replicas to fall seconds or minutes behind and serving stale reads.
failureModes.mitigation: Cap batch sizes (1,000–5,000 rows), sleep 50–200ms between chunks, and monitor `Seconds_Behind_Source` / `pg_stat_replication` to auto-pause.

failureModes.name: Incompatible Rolling-Deploy Schema
failureModes.description: Dropping or renaming a column in the same deploy as the code change breaks v1 pods still serving in-flight requests during a rolling update.
failureModes.mitigation: Strictly follow Expand -> Backfill -> Switch Reads -> Contract across separate deployments.

failureModes.name: Invalid Index Left Behind by Failed CONCURRENTLY
failureModes.description: If `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` fails (e.g., due to a duplicate key in a `UNIQUE` index), Postgres leaves an `INVALID` index that still incurs write overhead without serving queries.
failureModes.mitigation: Query `pg_index WHERE NOT indisvalid`, drop the invalid index with `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, fix data, and recreate.

commonMistakes: Running `CREATE INDEX` without `CONCURRENTLY` on a live PostgreSQL table, locking out all writes for the entire index build.
Adding a `NOT NULL` column with a volatile default (or without `NOT VALID` check constraint on older engines) and triggering a full-table rewrite.
Forgetting to dual-write or backfill rows created between the Expand migration and the code rollout.
Running `gh-ost` or `pg_repack` when the database volume has less than 50% free disk space.
Leaving ORM auto-migrations (`hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=update`) enabled in production, causing unpredictable DDL locks on app startup.

sections.content:
## The idea

Online schema migrations decouple **schema evolution** from **application downtime** and **table locks**. Instead of mutating a live table in place while holding exclusive locks, you treat schema changes as a multi-phase state transition.

Two complementary mechanisms make this work:
1. **Expand-and-Contract (Parallel Change)** at the application/schema boundary, ensuring two consecutive app versions (`v1` and `v2`) are simultaneously compatible with the database.
2. **Non-blocking DDL & Shadow Table Copying** at the storage engine level (`gh-ost`, `pt-osc`, Vitess VReplication, or Postgres `CONCURRENTLY` / `NOT VALID`), ensuring writes never stall during multi-hour data copies.

## Concrete walkthrough

Suppose we need to change `orders.total_amount` from `INT` to `BIGINT` on a 120M-row MySQL table running 8,000 QPS:

1. **Shadow Table Creation**: `gh-ost` creates `_orders_gho` with the new `BIGINT` column and connects as a fake replica to stream the MySQL binary log (`ROW` format).
2. **Chunked Backfill + Binlog Apply**: It copies primary-key ranges of 2,000 rows from `orders` to `_orders_gho` while continuously applying live `INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` events from the binlog. If replica lag exceeds 50ms, `gh-ost` throttles automatically.
3. **Atomic Cutover**: Once caught up, `gh-ost` acquires a brief metadata lock and executes `RENAME TABLE orders TO _orders_del, _orders_gho TO orders` in a few milliseconds.
4. **Verification & Cleanup**: After confirming error rates and latency remain flat, `_orders_del` is dropped.

sections.content:
## The Expand-and-Contract lifecycle

Even when DDL itself is non-blocking, **semantic changes** (renaming columns, splitting fields, changing enum meanings) require four distinct phases:

1. **Expand**: Add the new nullable column or table (`first_name`, `last_name`) alongside the old one (`full_name`).
2. **Dual-Write & Backfill**: Deploy `v2` code that writes both old and new columns while reading from the old. Run a throttled background job to backfill historical rows.
3. **Switch Reads**: Deploy `v3` code that reads from the new column (still dual-writing to allow instant rollback).
4. **Contract**: Deploy `v4` to stop writing the old column, then drop the old column.

## Engine-specific online DDL primitives

| Operation | MySQL 8.0 Native (`ALGORITHM=INSTANT/INPLACE`) | `gh-ost` (MySQL) | PostgreSQL 14+ Safe Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Add Nullable Column** | `INSTANT` (metadata only, <10ms) | Not needed | `ADD COLUMN` + `lock_timeout = '2s'` |
| **Change Column Type** | `COPY` (blocks writes) | Safe via shadow table | Expand-and-Contract (new col + backfill) |
| **Create Index** | `INPLACE` (concurrent DML) | N/A | `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` |
| **Add NOT NULL / FK** | `COPY` / `INPLACE` | Safe via shadow table | `ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID` -> `VALIDATE` |
| **Primary Risk** | Metadata Lock (MDL) pileup | Disk space (2x) + no FKs | `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` queue starvation |

## Failure modes

1. **Metadata Lock (MDL) Starvation**: In both MySQL and Postgres, a DDL waiting on a 30-second reporting query blocks all *subsequent* short queries behind it. Always set `lock_timeout` (Postgres) or `lock_wait_timeout` (MySQL) to 1–3 seconds and retry.
2. **Disk Exhaustion on Shadow Copies**: Cloning a 400 GB table on a 500 GB volume triggers an emergency read-only filesystem halt. Verify >= 2.2x table size in free storage before starting.
3. **Broken Rollbacks After Early Contract**: Dropping the old column before verifying `v3` stability makes rolling back a bad deployment impossible without restoring backups.

## Practical checklist

- **Set `lock_timeout` on every migration**: Default to `2s` in Postgres and `2s` `lock_wait_timeout` in MySQL.
- **Never use `CREATE INDEX` without `CONCURRENTLY`** in Postgres (and run it outside a transaction block).
- **Throttle backfills**: Chunk by primary key (1,000–5,000 rows), sleep between batches, and halt if replica lag > 100ms.
- **Check disk headroom**: Confirm free disk exceeds `2x` the target table + index size before running `gh-ost` or `pg_repack`.
- **Separate schema from code deploys**: Keep old and new schemas compatible across at least one full deployment cycle.

interviewProblems.title: Online Schema Migrations
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Online Schema Migrations. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Techniques for altering tables, indexes, and constraints on live production databases without taking downtime or blocking application reads and writes.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: gh-ost + Shadow Table applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Read Replica Monitor.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Read Replica Monitor experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Enforce `SET lock_timeout = '2000ms'` and `SET statement_timeout = '5000ms'` in migration runners, retrying with backoff if a lock cannot be acquired.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Never run a blocking `ALTER TABLE` directly on a large table; pair the Expand-and-Contract pattern with online shadow-table tools (`gh-ost`) or Postgres lock-safe primitives (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `lock_timeout`).
Avoid trap: Running `CREATE INDEX` without `CONCURRENTLY` on a live PostgreSQL table, locking out all writes for the entire index build.
Avoid trap: Adding a `NOT NULL` column with a volatile default (or without `NOT VALID` check constraint on older engines) and triggering a full-table rewrite.
When to reach for it: Altering tables exceeding a few million rows or several gigabytes in MySQL/InnoDB or PostgreSQL where table rewrites take minutes to hours.
When to reach for it: Zero-downtime deployments using rolling or blue/green releases where old (v1) and new (v2) application pods run concurrently against the same schema.

putItTogether.title: Putting Online Schema Migrations Together
putItTogether.summary: Never run a blocking `ALTER TABLE` directly on a large table; pair the Expand-and-Contract pattern with online shadow-table tools (`gh-ost`) or Postgres lock-safe primitives (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `lock_timeout`).
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Online Schema Migrations before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Using `gh-ost` with `--max-lag-millis=50` and `--chunk-size=2000`, the team copied the table over 4.5 hours during off-peak traffic, dual-wrote in app code for 48 hours, and executed an atomic cutover with p99 latency remaining under 18ms.
